expected_direction: Higher risk-axis scores should indicate larger burden on the measured row.
implemented_direction: The risk axis raises scores for rows with worse matched financing or cashflow pressure and yields dreamus=75.000000 versus spotify=25.000000 in mus_streaming_paid_core.
notes: The streaming risk axis remains partial but no hidden sign inversion was found.

expected_direction: Higher market-axis scores should indicate larger market-side burden on the measured row.
implemented_direction: The market axis uses a conservative rule under which Korean rows can receive zero or lower concentration burden when the Korean proxy market is locally concentrated while global rows can still receive positive burden; streaming rows are kakao_ent=33.333333 dreamus=25.000000 spotify=25.149377.
notes: This axis is directionally disciplined but not a clean same-service paid-share burden measure because it relies on proxy construction.

expected_direction: Missing reg-axis coverage should lower admissibility rather than silently preserve a stable three-axis headline interpretation.
implemented_direction: The composite builder reweights only observed axes equally and gives one-axis rows full weight 1.0 so kakao_ent becomes a full-value market-only composite at 33.333333.
notes: The code is explicit and arithmetically consistent but headline meaning is overstated because thin rows can look comparable to two-axis rows.

expected_direction: If the composite cleanly measures Korean disadvantage then a positive korea_minus_global_gap should mean Korean rows are more burdened than global peers.
implemented_direction: The gap output script computes korea_minus_global_gap as literal korean_mean minus global_mean and labels positive values as korean_higher.
notes: The arithmetic sign is correct but the headline interpretation is unstable because the Korean mean includes a fallback thin row and the global side is a single peer.
